original.reason: The Sylow counts force either a unique Sylow subgroup or the simultaneous exceptional counts. In the exceptional case, eight distinct order-7 Sylow subgroups contribute 48 nonidentity elements of order 7; a Sylow 2-subgroup supplies 8 disjoint elements, and any distinct Sylow 2-subgroup supplies an additional element not among those, yielding a contradiction.
